title: Why Does Hinduism Have No Single Founder?

titles.option_a_curiosity: Why Does Hinduism Have No Single Founder?

detected_concept: Hinduism as its followers understand it
description:
What if one of the world's oldest living religions had no founder at all? This short explains how followers understand Hinduism, from its sacred texts to its festivals.

Hinduism has no single founder and no single central authority. It is an ancient, very diverse tradition with more than a billion followers, and its sacred texts include the Vedas, the Upanishads and the Bhagavad Gita. Hindus believe in dharma, the duty and right way of living, karma, the results of our actions, and samsara, the cycle of rebirth. The aim is moksha, liberation from that cycle. Many paths are honored, and people pray at home and in temples and celebrate festivals such as Diwali and Holi.

Which of these ideas, dharma, karma or moksha, was new to you?
